title: One Scale, Four Texts: Gaps, Overlaps and Silent Repairs in Published Grading Schemes
abstract: arXiv:2611.06569v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Category systems often reach their users as text, and readers apply them with tacit repairs. We ask what such a text determines once the repairs are removed, using diabetic retinopathy grading, where one international scale circulates in several documents. We transcribe four texts (the English screening definitions of 2025, the international scale as tabulated in 2017 and as published in 2003, and an Italian guideline of 2015) into one rule language over 24 finding variables, and make every point a text leaves open a named precisification. Exhaustive enumeration of 1,425,807,360 finding profiles, re-derived by an SMT solver and spot-checked by an OWL reasoner, shows that every text that assigns actions leaves some eyes without a category under every reading; that the 2017 tabulation has a proliferative class that is empty when read literally and a macular gap that the 2003 text lacks, so that no function maps the 2003 grades onto the 201

translated_title: 一个量表，四种文本：已发表分级方案中的缺口、重叠与静默修补
translated_abstract: 类别系统通常以文本形式传递到用户手中，而读者在应用时会对其进行心照不宣的修补。我们以糖尿病视网膜病变分级为研究对象，探讨一旦移除这些修补，此类文本本身究竟规定了什么；在该领域中，同一个国际量表以多份文档的形式流传。我们将四份文本（2025年的英文筛查定义、2017年制表版与2003年发表版的国际量表，以及2015年的一份意大利指南）转录为一种基于24个发现变量的统一规则语言，并将每份文本遗留的每一个未决之处都命名为一个明确的精确化。通过对1,425,807,360个发现特征组合的穷举枚举（由SMT求解器重新推导并经OWL推理器抽查验证），结果表明：任何赋予处置动作的文本，在任何解读下都会使某些眼睛得不到类别归属；2017年制表版存在一个按字面解读为空的增殖期类别，以及一个2003年文本所没有的黄斑缺口，因而不存在任何函数能将2003年的分级映射到201……
tldr: 该论文将糖尿病视网膜病变分级的四份权威文本统一形式化为基于24个发现变量的规则语言，并通过对14亿余个病例组合的穷举枚举首次严格证明：每份文本在任何解读下都存在无法归类的病例，且2003版与2017版之间存在无法互相映射的类别缺口。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes four authoritative texts of the diabetic retinopathy grading scale into a single rule language over 24 finding variables and, through exhaustive enumeration of over 1.4 billion finding profiles, proves that every text leaves some eyes uncategorizable under every reading and that the 2003 and 2017 versions contain grades that cannot be mapped onto each other.
